canonical_name: Hilbert's theorem on complete surfaces of constant negative Gaussian curvature
source_claim_verbatim_translation: A complete surface of constant negative curvature cannot be isometrically immersed in R^3.
canonical_statement: Provisional modern scope: there is no sufficiently regular isometric immersion into Euclidean three-space of a complete two-dimensional Riemannian manifold having constant Gaussian curvature -1. The exact regularity, connectedness, and completeness formulation must be reconciled with Hilbert's analytic-surface hypotheses before the statement gate.
domain_and_universes: A two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M and a map f : M -> EuclideanSpace Real (Fin 3); exact Lean universes, manifold model, and regularity classes are not frozen at intake.
quantifiers: for every two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M satisfying the selected connectedness and regularity assumptions
for every map f from M to Euclidean three-space having the selected immersion regularity
hypotheses: M is complete for its Riemannian distance (subject to source-equivalence audit)
the Gaussian/sectional curvature of M is constantly -1
f pulls the Euclidean metric back to the Riemannian metric on M
conclusion: No such isometric immersion f exists.

alternate_encodings.target: No everywhere regular analytic surface in R^3 of constant Gaussian curvature -1 satisfying Hilbert's global finite-accumulation condition
alternate_encodings.relationship: primary-source formulation; equivalence or implication to the modern complete-manifold formulation is not yet checked

alternate_encodings.target: The same nonimmersion claim for an arbitrary negative constant K < 0
alternate_encodings.relationship: scaling-equivalent candidate after metric and ambient dilation transports

alternate_encodings.target: Efimov-type nonimmersion under curvature bounded above by a negative constant
alternate_encodings.relationship: strict generalization, not a substitute target

boundary_and_exclusions: Local patches and incomplete surfaces are not ruled out.
Immersions into dimensions greater than three are outside the root claim.
Topological immersions or metric embeddings without the differential isometry condition are outside scope.
Positive or zero curvature is not included.
Efimov's variable-curvature theorem must not replace Hilbert's constant-curvature claim.
The regularity class is deliberately unresolved rather than silently strengthened from Hilbert's analytic surface to a modern C2 statement.
